about: Psalm 25:6–12 in the Vulgate numbering (Psalm 26 in Hebrew), said during the washing of hands. At Masses for the Dead, and at Masses of the season from Passion Sunday through Maundy Thursday, the Glória Patri is omitted. The psalm itself remains.

seg.nr: The priest washes his fingertips, the thumb and forefinger, while saying the psalm.

seg.tr: I will wash my hands among the innocent and go around Your altar, O Lord,

fn.w003: An adjective used as a noun in the accusative plural after “inter” (w002).
fn.w004: Accusative plural as the object of “Lavábo” (w001).

seg.tr: that I may hear the voice of praise and recount all Your wonders.

fn.w011: It opens a purpose clause with verbs in the subjunctive.
fn.w012: First-person singular subjunctive in the clause introduced by “Ut” (w011).
fn.w016: The second subjunctive verb governed by “Ut” (w011).
fn.w018: A neuter plural adjective used as a noun.

seg.tr: O Lord, I have loved the beauty of Your house and the place where Your glory dwells.

fn.w028: A genitive dependent on “habitatiónis” (w027), which itself depends on “locum” (w026).

seg.tr: O God, do not destroy my soul with the wicked, nor my life with bloodthirsty men,

fn.w033: An adjective used as a noun in the ablative plural after “cum” (w032).

seg.tr: whose hands hold iniquity and whose right hand is full of bribes.

fn.w044: The relative pronoun refers to “viris” (w039) in the preceding verse.
fn.w051: With “repléta” (w050), it forms a perfect passive.

seg.tr: But I have walked in innocence; redeem me and have mercy on me.

fn.w053: Nominative, expressed in contrast with the men described before.
fn.w058: Latin builds this perfect from a participle and the verb to be. Polish renders it in one word, so the auxiliary has no separate counterpart there.
fn.w059: With “ingréssus” (w058), it forms the perfect of a deponent verb.

seg.tr: My foot has stood on level ground; in the assemblies I will bless You, O Lord.

fn.w069: A neuter adjective used as a noun after “in” (w068).

seg.tr: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

fn.w075: Nominative in a verbless doxology: “glory be” is understood.

seg.tr: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
